Nilesh Narwekar: 
Thank you, Kunal, and good morning to all. Quarter 2 FY27 has seen a challenging external 
environment, marked by geopolitical uncertainties arising from the ongoing West Asia crisis 
and weaker monsoon, which has impacted the broader operating environment. However, the 
underlying fundamentals of the Indian economy remain resilient, supported by healthy GDP 
growth, sustained government capital expenditure and infrastructure activity continuing to 
support cement demand.

We remain constructive on the demand outlook for the balance of the year, particularly as 
infrastructure execution and construction activity gather pace. We've seen robust cement 
demand during the quarter, and this has supported price increases across our markets in 
September and October. With fuel and other input costs remaining elevated, we expect these 
price increases to sustain and support the company's margins. 
I would also like to highlight our continued momentum in the North region. Utilization at this 
plant has increased to 75% during the quarter. We are also continuing our dealer network 
expansion, while focusing on product quality, service levels and cost reduction initiatives.  
Happy to announce that at Nagaur, we have achieved EBITDA breakeven in quarter 2. The 
additional 1 million ton per annum grinding capacity commissioned in October further 
strengthens our ability to serve this region, and our costs will continue to reduce over the 
coming quarters. 
As I had highlighted in our previous calls, we have received several project approvals on the 
demand side, which are reflected in the current quarter's numbers for GGBS volumes which 
has grown by 7% Y-o-Y. The business continues to witness encouraging momentum, driven 
by growing demand from infrastructure and the RMC sector. 
Moving to the key operational highlights for quarter 2 FY27. Firstly, on volumes. Our total 
volume increased very strongly by 26% Y-o-Y to 3.93 million tons, which is among the 
highest in the industry. Taking this product-wise, cement volumes sold was 2.29 million metric 
tons, increased by almost 40% Y-o-Y. We saw good momentum in both channel and the B2B 
segment. Giving the comparative, if I was to exclude the North operations, cement volumes 
grew by around 13% Y-o-Y. GGBS volumes grew by 7% Y-o-Y, as I already mentioned. 
I also wanted to touch on realizations as shown in our presentation. Cement realization for 
quarter 2 FY27 was INR4,781 per ton, an increase of 3% Y-o-Y, but a softening of 3% 
quarter-on-quarter. We saw a decline in prices across regions in the early part of the quarter. 
But as I mentioned in my opening remarks, cement prices have increased across zones in 
September in the latter half and of course, in October. GGBS realizations for quarter 2 FY27 
was INR3,749 a ton. We would consider this a normal variation due to mix, and we continue 
to maintain our strategy of stable pricing.  
Within cement, trade mix remained stable at 52%. Our clinker-to-cement factor increased to 
58% with the ramp-up of North operations, especially as we currently are selling a higher 
quantity of OPC to maximize our kiln usage. Lead distance increased by 9 kilometers in the 
quarter to 294 kilometers. 
Lastly, I would also like to briefly touch on the capacity expansion program. As committed, 
during quarter 2, we commissioned the waste heat recovery system and the alternate fuel 
rehandling co-processing system in the Nagaur Integrated Unit. Early this month, we also 
commissioned the additional 1 MTPA grinding capacity at Nagaur and the overland belt 
conveyor for transporting limestone from the crusher to our plant.

These initiatives are expected to substantially reduce our cost in quarter 3 and quarter 4. In 
addition to the Nagaur WHRS unit, we added 36 megawatt of wind capacity in quarter 2 at 
Nandyal and Vijayanagar. And together, this has increased our green power share to 41% in 
quarter 2. 
Let me now hand over to Narinder to take you through the key financial highlights. 
Narinder Kahlon: 
Good morning. I will summarize the performance of Q2. Consolidated revenue was INR1,912 
crores. That's an increase of 33% year-on-year and 0.8% quarter-on-quarter, despite this being 
a monsoon quarter. 
Consolidated operating EBITDA was INR278 crores. That's an improvement of 4% year-on-
year. We saw improvement in realization in both cement and GGBS year-on-year. However, 
both fuel and packing costs also increased on a Y-o-Y basis. Consolidated operating EBITDA 
per ton was INR708 for the quarter. 
As has already been mentioned, the company achieved EBITDA breakeven in North in this 
quarter with a slightly positive EBITDA contribution. Excluding the North region, on a like-
for-like basis, revenue grew 14% Y-o-Y in Q2, while operating EBITDA increased by 3% Y-
o-Y to INR275 crores, which equates to INR821 per ton. 
On a consolidated basis, total EBITDA, including other income, was INR295 crores. PBT was 
INR101 crores during the quarter, including positive contribution of nearly INR20 crores from 
JV. PAT for the quarter was about INR77 crores. 
In terms of the trend in the main cost elements during the quarter, raw material and power and 
fuel decreased by 2% quarter-on-quarter with slightly higher fuel cost on a Q-o-Q basis, offset 
by product mix changes. Blended fuel costs increased slightly from INR1.80 per MCal in the 
first quarter to INR1.84 per MCal in this quarter. As all of you are aware, pet coke prices are at 
very high levels, and this will create more cost pressure in the coming quarter. But we are 
actively working towards increasing our share of domestic fuel and optimize our costs.  
Logistic cost was stable on a Q-on-Q basis with the impact of higher lead distance offset by 
savings from the railway busy season surcharge waiver and reallocation of volumes between 
Vijayanagar and Dolvi plants. Employee and other expenses per ton were stable on Q-o-Q 
basis. 
In terms of balance sheet, net debt was INR4,287 crores at the end of September. Net debt to 
EBITDA stood at 3.2x. Average cost of debt for the quarter was stable quarter-on-quarter at 
7.67%. The company incurred capex of INR483 crores during the quarter and INR820 crores 
during the first half of the year. This is the cash outgo, though the capex number will be 
slightly higher. 
 
We will be happy to address your questions now. Thank you.
